concepts.name: Functional versus non-functional requirements
concepts.summary: Distinguish what a system must do from qualities like latency, availability and scale, and clarify both before designing.

concepts.name: Client-server request flow
concepts.summary: Explain how a user request travels from client through DNS, load balancer, application servers and data store and back.

concepts.name: Vertical versus horizontal scaling
concepts.summary: Explain the difference between adding power to one machine and adding more machines, and the limits of each.

concepts.name: Latency, throughput and availability
concepts.summary: Define latency, throughput and availability and state the units used to express each.

concepts.name: Stateless application servers
concepts.summary: Explain why keeping session state out of app servers makes them easy to replicate and replace.

concepts.name: Load balancer role
concepts.summary: Describe how a load balancer spreads requests over servers and removes unhealthy ones.

concepts.name: Cache purpose
concepts.summary: Explain that a cache stores frequently read data in fast storage to cut latency and database load.

misconceptions.text: Scaling a system just means buying a bigger server.
Adding more servers automatically makes a system faster and more available.
A design can start immediately without asking clarifying questions about requirements.

concepts.name: Back-of-envelope capacity estimation
concepts.summary: Estimate QPS, storage and bandwidth from user counts, usage rates and object sizes using powers of ten.

concepts.name: Read-heavy versus write-heavy workloads
concepts.summary: Use the read-to-write ratio of a product to decide where to focus optimisation.

concepts.name: Load balancing algorithms
concepts.summary: Choose between round robin, least connections and hashing for a given traffic pattern.

concepts.name: Cache-aside and write strategies
concepts.summary: Apply cache-aside, write-through and write-back patterns and describe what each does on reads and writes.

concepts.name: Cache eviction policies
concepts.summary: Explain how LRU, LFU and TTL decide what to remove from a full cache.

concepts.name: CDN for static content
concepts.summary: Decide which assets to serve from edge locations to cut latency for distant users.

concepts.name: SQL versus NoSQL selection
concepts.summary: Pick a relational or NoSQL store based on data model, query patterns and scale needs.

concepts.name: API design for services
concepts.summary: Define simple endpoints, parameters and responses for a product's core operations.

misconceptions.text: Estimation must be exact to be useful.
A cache always returns correct, current data.
NoSQL is always faster and more scalable than a relational database.

concepts.name: Database replication topologies
concepts.summary: Set up leader-follower and multi-leader replication and explain read scaling and failover behaviour.

concepts.name: Sharding strategies
concepts.summary: Compare range, hash and directory-based partitioning and their effects on hotspots and queries.

concepts.name: Consistent hashing
concepts.summary: Use a hash ring with virtual nodes to add or remove nodes while moving little data.

concepts.name: Message queues and async processing
concepts.summary: Decouple producers from consumers with queues to absorb bursts and handle slow work asynchronously.

concepts.name: CAP theorem trade-offs
concepts.summary: Analyse how a system must trade consistency against availability when a network partition occurs.

concepts.name: Consistency models
concepts.summary: Distinguish strong and eventual consistency and judge which a feature can tolerate.

concepts.name: Unique ID generation
concepts.summary: Generate unique, roughly sortable IDs across many servers without a single bottleneck.

concepts.name: Indexing and denormalisation trade-offs
concepts.summary: Analyse when indexes or duplicated data speed up reads at the cost of write complexity.

misconceptions.text: CAP means you pick any two of three properties at all times.
Replicas make a database both faster for writes and fully consistent.
Hashing keys with modulo N is fine when nodes are added or removed.

concepts.name: Hotspot and skew mitigation
concepts.summary: Diagnose uneven load from popular keys and mitigate it with key splitting, caching or fan-out changes.

concepts.name: Fan-out on write versus read
concepts.summary: Evaluate push, pull and hybrid feed generation against follower counts and freshness needs.

concepts.name: Delivery semantics and idempotency
concepts.summary: Judge at-most-once, at-least-once and effectively-once processing and design idempotent consumers.

concepts.name: Cache stampede and invalidation
concepts.summary: Analyse cache invalidation risks and prevent stampedes with locking, request coalescing or jittered TTLs.

concepts.name: Failure handling patterns
concepts.summary: Evaluate timeouts, retries with backoff, circuit breakers and load shedding to stop cascading failures.

concepts.name: Real-time communication design
concepts.summary: Compare polling, long polling and persistent connections for chat or notifications, including presence and ordering.

concepts.name: Quorum reads and writes
concepts.summary: Evaluate quorum settings to balance consistency, latency and availability in replicated stores.

concepts.name: Capacity and bottleneck analysis
concepts.summary: Use estimates to find the first component to saturate and justify the next scaling step.

misconceptions.text: Retrying failed requests always improves reliability.
Exactly-once delivery is achievable by the broker alone without idempotent consumers.
Fan-out on write is always better for news feeds.

concepts.name: Conflict resolution strategies
concepts.summary: Evaluate last-write-wins, vector clocks and CRDTs for reconciling concurrent writes.

concepts.name: Multi-region architecture design
concepts.summary: Design active-active or active-passive multi-region systems with explicit latency, conflict and failover plans.

concepts.name: Trade-off justification under constraints
concepts.summary: Weigh alternatives against stated requirements, cost and team capacity, and defend the choice with numbers.

concepts.name: Evolutionary scaling roadmap
concepts.summary: Create a staged path from a simple single-region design to a large-scale one with triggers for each step.

concepts.name: SLO-driven reliability design
concepts.summary: Derive SLOs and error budgets from user needs and design redundancy, observability and degradation to meet them.

concepts.name: Distributed transactions and sagas
concepts.summary: Evaluate two-phase commit, sagas and the outbox pattern for cross-service data integrity.

concepts.name: Cost and efficiency optimisation
concepts.summary: Assess storage tiering, compression and compute choices to reduce cost without breaking requirements.

concepts.name: Novel system composition
concepts.summary: Combine known building blocks to design a system for an unfamiliar problem and test it against failure scenarios.

misconceptions.text: Two-phase commit is a cheap way to get cross-service consistency at any scale.
Last-write-wins is safe because it never loses data.
A good design should include every scaling technique from the start.
